extracted.intended_audience: PTAB panel members, Director's staff, and patent practitioners (petitioners and patent owners)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards governing how the Patent Trial and Appeal Board must handle contested evidence, motions to exclude, and related reasoning when issuing (or being reviewed on) final written decisions in inter partes review proceedings. Focused on vacatur/remand and requirements for addressing evidence relevant to an obviousness/motivation-to-combine analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board must decide dispositive issues properly
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board must decide dispositive issues properly before it, even if they are contrary to its ultimate conclusion. (See Parus Holdings, Inc. v. Google LLC, 70 F.4th 1365, 1372 (Fed. Cir. 2023).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a dispositive issue (e.g., motivation to combine in an obviousness inquiry) is presented, the Board must address it on the merits rather than leaving it unaddressed; failure to do so can be reversible error and may require vacatur and remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: When evidence is contested, the Board must either consider it or exclude it
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board should have either (i) considered Patent Owner’s evidence ... when determining whether Petitioner has sufficiently established a motivation to combine the cited references, or (ii) excluded the evidence in response to Petitioner’s Motion to Exclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may not ignore contested, properly-submitted evidence and nonetheless dismiss arguments based on that evidence; it must affirmatively decide whether to admit and weigh the evidence or exclude it, explaining the basis for that decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: For any evidence considered, address impact on the obviousness analysis and the weight to be given
rubrics_metrics.description: For any evidence that is considered, the Board should address the impact (if any) of the evidence on the obviousness analysis (including the weight that should be given) and provide a reasoned explanation to support its determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board admits contested exhibits, it must explain how (and to what extent) they affect findings such as motivation to combine, material teachings, or secondary considerations, and articulate the weight assigned to each piece of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board must evaluate disputed exhibits in relation to motions to exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner moved to exclude most of this evidence as inadmissible under the Federal Rules of Evidence. The Board dismissed Petitioner’s Motion to Exclude as moot because the Board 'did not rely on any of the contested evidence.' That explanation did not adequately address the disputed evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a party moves to exclude exhibits (e.g., on FRE grounds), the Board should either rule on admissibility or otherwise justify why the evidence will not be considered; a mere statement of 'we do not rely on the evidence' is insufficient when the evidence is relied on in arguments the Board resolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness/motivation-to-combine findings must account for contemporaneous industry evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Owner introduced contemporaneous documentary evidence that showed those of skill in the industry would not have combined the prior art. The Board failed to evaluate Patent Owner’s disputed exhibits for its arguments regarding motivation to combine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parties present contemporaneous industry documents relevant to whether a person of ordinary skill would have been motivated to combine references, the Board should consider that evidence's probative value and explain its effect (if any) on the motivation-to-combine analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Board is not required to discuss every exhibit or argument
rubrics_metrics.description: My decision here should not be mistaken as requiring that the Board must discuss every exhibit in the record or argument however cursory. See Parus Holdings, 70 F.4th at 1372 (noting that the Board does not have to 'review evidence and issues introduced by a party in violation of its rules or not introduced at all').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The obligation to explain decisions is bounded: the Board need not analyze exhibits or arguments that were not properly before it or that were introduced in violation of procedural rules; focus explanation on properly submitted, material evidence and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of explanation for excluding vs. not relying on evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board’s statement that it did not rely on any of the contested evidence and therefore dismissed the motion to exclude as moot was inadequate; the Board must provide a reasoned explanation when it effectively rejects evidence-based arguments without expressly excluding the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board intends not to rely on contested evidence, it should either (a) explicitly exclude the evidence with an admissibility ruling or (b) explicitly consider the evidence and explain why it gives it no weight; perfunctory dismissal is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand remedy when Board fails to address contested evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: I vacate the Board’s Final Written Decision and remand to the Board for further proceedings consistent with this Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Director (or appellate authority) finds the Board did not adequately address contested evidence relevant to a dispositive issue, the appropriate remedy is vacatur of the Final Written Decision and remand for the Board to either exclude or consider the evidence and to provide reasoned findings about its impact.
